what_it_does: Modern chips are built by bonding multiple smaller chiplets together using tiny copper connections—a process called copper-copper hybrid bonding. This paper addresses the problem that manufacturing these bonds is unreliable due to several failure modes: slight misalignment between bonding layers, particles contaminating the bond surface, uneven copper heights, rough wafer surfaces, and inconsistent copper density. The authors developed YAP, a mathematical model that can rapidly predict how many chips will successfully bond without needing slow computer simulations. Their model runs 10,000 times faster than traditional simulation approaches while still accounting for all five major failure mechanisms.
